findings.title: "What no longer has a guard anywhere: Nothing" is false — at least four assertions from the five deleted suites have neither a successor case nor a retired-class entry, and the head commit message repeats the claim.
findings.arbiter_reasoning: Measured, not inferred. M17 and M18 are confirmed survivors of mutations that the deleted suites' own assertions would have caught: migration-048-impersonation-sessions.test.ts asserted `expires_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL`, `ticket_id TEXT NOT NULL` and `reason TEXT NOT NULL`, and migration-051-structure.test.ts's `does not drop or mutate data` case banned `UPDATE`/`DELETE`/`DROP TABLE` in the file. None of the four appears in the new suites (048 pins four index definitions, three FK definitions and the `id` default and no column inventory; 051's row case covers only flagged_responses rows), none appears in the three 'genuinely retired' classes at :110-130, and a repo-wide search finds no other assertion covering them. The doc's closing sentence is the answer to the exact question ci:weakened-checks raised, so a reviewer reading it stops looking. Fix is small: name the four under the retired-classes section with a reason, or add the two missing oracle-A pins (048 column inventory; a row assertion or a static no-DML ban).

findings.title: Lost coverage: no suite anywhere asserts impersonation_sessions column nullability, so loosening `expires_at NOT NULL` in migration 048 passes every gate.
findings.arbiter_reasoning: M17 survived 5/5, and it survives in the re-provisioned world too because no oracle-A literal pins the inventory. 048 is the odd sibling: migration-051-...:190-215 pins a full 14-column inventory and migration-117-...:492-515 pins a full ten-column inventory. The property is the time-box on an admin view-as session. Cheapest fix: add the impersonation_sessions column inventory to 048's head-posture case, matching its two siblings.

findings.title: Lost coverage: off-target DML. `assertOnlyTablesMoved` compares the catalogue only, so an unrelated `UPDATE`/`DELETE` appended to any of the seven migrations passes every suite.
findings.arbiter_reasoning: M18 survived 5/5 with `UPDATE accounts SET display_name = ...` appended to 051. The deleted 051 and 053 suites carried crude text bans for exactly this class. Only 051 and 053 make any row assertion, and each covers only its own table's rows. Either restore a static no-DML ban for the six migrations that declare no DML (053 is the one exception, and it is the only DML in the set), or add a row-count/whole-row check over the parent tables each suite already seeds.

findings.title: Off-target blind spot: `readPublicCatalogue` never reads `pg_default_acl`, so appending `ALTER DEFAULT PRIVILEGES IN SCHEMA public GRANT ALL ON TABLES TO anon, authenticated;` to any of the seven migrations passes every suite.
findings.arbiter_reasoning: M19 survived 4/4. This is the statement migration 118's own degrade uses (migration-118-...:226-228) precisely because it makes every subsequently created table inherit client grants — so the change knows the statement is potent and still does not guard against a migration carrying it. The effect outlives the migration: every table created afterwards is open to anon and authenticated. `assertOnlyTablesMoved` can read it cheaply; migration-118-...:233-242 already has `readDefaultTableAcl`.

findings.title: Off-target blind spot: `readPublicCatalogue` filters `relkind IN ('r','p')`, so a migration that appends a view over a deny-all table plus a client-role GRANT re-opens the RLS boundary with every suite green.
findings.arbiter_reasoning: M20 survived 4/4, and the bypass is measured rather than argued: inside a rolled-back transaction on test_1301, with `CREATE VIEW public.analytics_events_leak AS SELECT * FROM analytics_events` plus `GRANT SELECT ... TO anon`, has_table_privilege('anon','public.analytics_events','SELECT') is false while `SET ROLE anon; SELECT count(*) FROM public.analytics_events_leak` returns 10 rows — a view defaults to security_invoker=false and runs as its owner, who bypasses RLS while FORCE is off. Supabase PostgREST exposes views, so this is the same exposure path migration 049 exists to close. Views, sequences, functions and triggers are all outside the catalogue; the helper's JSDoc framing ('arbitrary damage elsewhere') reads wider than the implementation. Either widen relkind and add nspacl/pg_default_acl, or state the boundary in the JSDoc and in each suite's stated limits.

findings.title: A production-file comment describes migration 118's degrade as "deny-all RLS off and the client-role privileges the migration revokes granted back" — it is neither, and the description hides the one degrade in the set that touches a schema-level object.
findings.arbiter_reasoning: 118's actual degrade (migration-118-poller-heartbeats.integration.test.ts:225-230) is `ALTER DEFAULT PRIVILEGES IN SCHEMA public GRANT ALL ON TABLES TO anon, authenticated;` followed by `DROP TABLE poller_heartbeats;`. It never disables RLS and never grants on the table. 118's own header calls the ALTER DEFAULT PRIVILEGES step the riskiest in #1301 and devotes a section to proving it rolls back; the registry comment that a future reader consults first says nothing about it and asserts two things that are false.

findings.title: A self-satisfying assertion with a false stated rationale, newly introduced in two suites: `expect(columnPrivileges).toHaveLength(4)` cannot fail if PostgreSQL adds a fifth column privilege.
findings.arbiter_reasoning: `columnPrivileges` is a hardcoded literal declared on the line above, so the assertion only restates its own input. The comment directly above claims 'the length assertion means a PostgreSQL that ever adds a fifth fails loudly rather than under-covering' — it would do nothing of the kind. The same pair appears at migration-118-poller-heartbeats.integration.test.ts:406-407, and neither existed at the merge-base (117's ARM A/B/C block is new in this change). Behavioural replacement: assert against a derived source, e.g. that `aclexplode(acldefault('c', <owner>))` is empty AND that the four names match a list read from `information_schema.column_privileges`-style introspection, or delete the assertion and keep only the honest comment that the four are fixed by the standard.

findings.title: `renderValue`'s separator JSDoc claims the two control characters "cannot occur in a catalogue name or definition"; U+0001 can appear in a PostgreSQL text comment, so two different comment lists can in principle render equal.
findings.arbiter_reasoning: U+0000 genuinely cannot appear in a PostgreSQL text value, so the FIELD separator is safe; U+0001 is an ordinary text character and `columnComments` / the table `comment` carry arbitrary text. Theoretical rather than reachable in this repo — no checked-in comment contains a control character — and the equality diffs in the suites are deep-equals on structured arrays rather than on renderValue, so only `assertOnlyTablesMoved` and the vacuity check use the rendering. Recorded because it is a stated impossibility that is not impossible; fix is to narrow the claim to U+0000 or to render with a length-prefixed encoding.
